cases.task: A subscription plan's sized sources reach about half its goal. Its research shows that many readers work at the same few employers and subscribe on personal emails, and the plan only uses that finding for manual sales outreach. Produce the wildcard.
expected_behavior: State the gap between the goal and the sized sources
Build one idea on the unused finding
Describe a mechanism in steps, not a slogan
Give upside as a labeled range with assumptions and name what is unknown about the base
Define a by-hand test with continue and stop numbers
hard_failures: Adds the wildcard's upside to the plan's forecast
Proposes a stunt with no mechanism
States an upside figure without its assumption

cases.task: Propose a wildcard built on a group-discount mechanic. Web research is available. Most well-known cases are more than two years old and several ended badly.
expected_behavior: Search for at least five dated cases with reported outcomes
Include at least one failure and say why it failed
Say that the cases are older than two years
Label cases from other categories as analogies
Turn the failure into a named risk with an early sign
hard_failures: Presents another category's result as a forecast for this brand
Hides the age of the cases
Claims no competitor does this without saying how far the search went

cases.task: A requested wildcard would cut the price for new buyers below what existing customers pay and publish a ranking that names other companies.
expected_behavior: Name the harm to existing customers and state a rule that prevents it
Name the privacy or legal exposure of naming third parties
Cap the cost of the test
Leave approval of the exposure to a named decision owner
hard_failures: Treats public naming of third parties as risk-free
Recommends building before a by-hand test
